# Whallm 1.1.12
Changes since v1.1.11.
## Use less memory with 8-bit resident weights
- Both Qwen models have a new setting, **Use 8-bit resident weights**, in **Model → Advanced Settings**. It is off by default. - When it is on, the weights that stay in memory, except experts, are kept in 8 bits instead of BF16. This uses less memory and usually speeds up output, most with MTP on. - Output can differ slightly from output with the setting off. - **Estimated peak memory** now drops when you turn the setting on. For Swift1.5 the estimate is about 3.7 GiB lower.
## New Qwen defaults
- **Experts in memory** now defaults to 8.5% (2,089 slots, about 5.1 GiB). It was about 12.5% (7.5 GiB). - **MTP experts in memory** now defaults to 100% (512 slots, about 1.2 GiB). It was about 8%. - Together, the two defaults use about 1.3 GiB less memory than before.
## Less work per token for Qwen
- Output no longer rebuilds each expert's weight views for every token. They are built once and reused. - When the main model checks MTP drafts, it no longer copies the whole attention history every round. - N-gram lookups ask macOS for all the pages they need at once instead of one at a time. - Loading reads large weights with four workers. - QSA index keys are stored once instead of twice.
Output tokens are unchanged by these five changes.
## DeepSeek V4.1
- Engram lookups ask macOS for all the pages they need at once, as Qwen N-gram lookups do.
## Upgrade notes
- The new defaults apply to new installs and when you reset a model's settings. Your saved settings are kept. - Prompt Cache entries saved with **Use 8-bit resident weights** on are kept apart from entries saved with it off.
## Benchmarks
Measured with the built-in **Throughput** test on a build from source shortly before this release: Swift1.5, MTP and **Use 8-bit resident weights** on, **Code** input, a 512-token output limit, 2,089 expert slots, temperature 0 and seed 42.
| Chip | Input tokens | TTFT (ms) | Prefill (tok/s) | Decode (tok/s) | Peak MLX (GiB) | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | M5 Pro | 4096 | 6976.5 | 587.1 | 19.4 | 13.13 | | M5 Pro | 8192 | 13911.4 | 588.9 | 19.8 | 13.86 | | M5 Pro | 16384 | 29654.2 | 552.5 | 18.6 | 14.29 | | M2 Max | 4096 | 15151.2 | 270.3 | 15.0 | 13.15 | | M2 Max | 8192 | 30693.5 | 266.9 | 15.8 | 13.84 | | M2 Max | 16384 | 65538.0 | 250.0 | 14.7 | 14.42 |
The v1.1.11 run on the same M5 Pro peaked at 16.93 to 18.81 GiB and produced 14.6 to 17.5 tokens per second. That run used a 128-token output limit and did not have 8-bit resident weights, so this is not a controlled comparison.
## Validation
- **719 Python tests passed**; **195 Swift tests ran, with 4 skipped and no failures**. - Packaging checks cover signatures, bundled files and startup in English, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese without access to the build folder, for both the App and the unzipped download.
## Known limits
- **Estimated peak memory** was about 2 GiB higher than the measured peak in the runs above. The estimate includes a safety allowance and memory that MLX holds for reuse; the measured number does not. - The lower estimate for 8-bit resident weights is calculated from the model's file list. It was compared with measurements only for Swift1.5. - There are no measurements for Qwen3.8 FP8 with 8-bit resident weights. - The benchmark rows come from one M5 Pro and one M2 Max.
Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 15 or later. Model weights are downloaded separately. This is a distribution build; local-only debug and Dry run features are not included.
[Full changelog](https://github.com/yanun0323/Whallm/compare/v1.1.11...v1.1.12)

## Whallm 1.1.7-dev.2 — Alpha
This alpha adds a Throughput benchmark page and updates model defaults. Select **dev** in **Settings → Updates** to receive it. Stable users continue to receive official releases only.
### Throughput benchmark
- Select an installed model and run the benchmark; the app loads the selected model automatically. - Choose **Code** or **Novel**. Both are bundled and work offline: a Whallm source snapshot and Herman Melville's *Moby-Dick*. Each contains enough tokens for 200K inputs with all three supported tokenizers, without repeating a short excerpt. - Select one or more context lengths from **1K to 200K**, with a generation limit of **128, 1024, or 4096** tokens. - View first-token latency, time per output token, input/output speed, total time, throughput, and peak MLX memory. Results include the slots used by that run. - Copy results as **plain text, JSON, or a Markdown table**. The results table fills the available width, and settings controls align on the right. - Cancel a running benchmark and retain completed results. Tests run one request at a time with prompt reuse disabled; model loading and input tokenization are excluded from timing, and no extra warm-up is performed.
### Model settings
- **Max tokens now defaults to 8192 for every model**. Explicitly saved values remain unchanged; reset or edit Advanced Settings to change an existing preference.
### Validation and alpha limits
- Development checks passed 412 Python tests and 82 Swift tests. Three Swift tests require unavailable model fixtures and were skipped; the interactive Keychain round-trip test was excluded. - Packaging checks verify signatures, notarization, all three localizations, and isolated startup for both the app and an extracted ZIP copy. - **Dry run is available only in local builds.** This alpha excludes the simulated-results option and its generator. - Corpus coverage is an offline tokenizer check, not a measured 200K generation result. No new full-model speed or output-quality claim is made. Actual generation can end before the selected output limit. - DeepSeek V4.1 remains experimental and text-only; its previous unsupported features remain unchanged.
